items.Sentence: In the headworks, wastewater is filtered through dual bar screens with 3-millimeter openings, before being transferred to the main treatment system.
The filtered wastewater is collected in a 50,000 gallon underground fiberglass equalization tank with aeration to provide mixing.

From the equalization tank, the wastewater is then pumped into the anoxic basin inside the treatment plant building. The anoxic basin is sized for denitrification and has a mixer to maintain the solids in solution while not providing any air to the waste.

The current WWTF provides tertiary treatment that combines an activated sludge process, membranes to filter the wastewater, and ultraviolet (UV) disinfection. The flow is moved to the aerated membrane bioreactor (MBR) via pumps.
Within this system is the UV treatment process which acts as a disinfectant and is the last treatment step prior to dispersal.

Sludge separated from the effluent in the treatment process is dewatered using a centrifuge. The centrifuge acts as a de-watering process to separate suspended solids from the treated water prior to membrane filtration and disinfection.
Additionally, an existing centrifuge is utilized, as well as an off-board waste activated sludge (WAS) storage.
Filtered material captured in the screens is disposed of at the Mariposa County Sanitary Landfill.
In the winter, effluent is discharged to three leachfields, with a designed flow limit of 0.030 mgd or 30,000 gallons per day (gpd).
In the summer, when snow is not on the ground, in addition to the leachfields, a subsurface drip disposal system is available for use that by design adds another 0.050 mgd of disposal capacity.

DNC is also proposing to use recycled water for landscape irrigation in the summer months and submitted a Title 22 Report (Report) to the State Water Board, Division of Drinking Water (DDW) in March 2017.
DNC submitted Report of Waste Discharge – Amendment No. 2 on 6 February 2017 that proposes to add 908 linear feet of leachfield trench to the existing central leachfield.
The dual usage of the subsurface drip system along with a 150,000 gallon storage tank and the expanded leachfield should provide sufficient disposal capacity at the Tenaya Lodge.
DNC replaced the former secondary treatment WWTF in January of 2016 with a new tertiary WWTF.
